Subject: GCP private offer: 3yr commit + blended rev-share & invoicing exception

Team — forwarding NovaRetail's ask so we can get direction. Quick summary below; attached is their proposed financials (NovaRetail_Pricing_Summary.pdf).

What customer is asking:
- 3-year private offer (GCP marketplace) with a stepped usage commitment: $1.2M first-year ARR, then growth-based bands years 2–3.
- Rev-share ask: 20% year 1, 16% year 2, 12% year 3 (they've proposed this to us).
- Invoicing: procurement requires net90 terms and PO-based invoicing (legal will want this).
- Marketing co-sell commitment and joint case study required for the first 12 months.

Why this is an escalation:
- Rev-share above our standard marketplace guidance for private offers; multi-year stepped rev-share is nonstandard.
- Net90 + PO billing exposes us to credit risk and cash flow drag; typically we require net30/net45 or partial upfront.
- Customer is strategic (large retail account in our target segment) and has strong logo value for our channel motion.

Ask from deal desk:
- Karthik / Marissa, please advise recommended concession level and what approval path we need.
- If this requires exec signoff, can we get a succinct recommendation (numbers + mitigations) so I can present to Jonas?

Attachments: NovaRetail_Pricing_Summary.pdf (pricing worksheet), initial term sheet attached as Draft_Private_Offer_20261021.json

Thanks — Soojin

Subject: Re: GCP private offer: 3yr commit + blended rev-share & invoicing exception

Soojin — thanks for the detailed note and attachments. Quick take from Deal Desk after an initial read: 

1) Rev-share: 20% first-year is above our standard ceiling for comparable marketplace private offers. I would be comfortable recommending a 19% introductory rev-share year 1 but only if we secure one of the following mitigations:
   - 30% upfront invoice at signing (applied to Year 1), OR
   - Marketing/PR commitment with measurable milestones and a co-funded MDF credit of $50k in year 1.

2) Multi-year stepped rev-share is acceptable if we lock minimum committed spend per year and include a downward adjustment clause if they fail to hit their bands.

3) Invoicing terms: Net90 is a hard pass for us without credit coverage. Our preference is net30 or net60 with a PO + 30% upfront retainer. If Finance confirms we can stretch to net75 with a credit review and a purchase order guarantee, that could be a compromise, but it requires exec signoff.

4) Other nonstandard items: the joint case study ask is fine; legal will want approval for marketing language.

Recommended escalation package to present to execs: 
- Offer: 19% rev-share Y1 / 15% Y2 / 12% Y3 contingent on committed spend bands.
- Billing: PO + 30% upfront, remaining net60.
- Clawback: 12-month clawback on co-funded credits if customer churns or materially under-delivers.
- Validity: Approval window 72 hours from exec signoff to lock terms.

I'll coordinate with Finance (Ben) on the credit/term side. Marissa, please pull the draft private offer and the revenue ops view on forecast impact so we can present clean numbers to Jonas.

-Karthik

Jonas — forwarding the thread and our recommended exception package for signoff. TL;DR recommendation below; full details and attachments are in the thread.

Recommendation (for exec approval):
- Approve a one-time exception: 19% rev-share year 1 / 15% year 2 / 12% year 3.
- Billing exception: Accept PO-based invoicing with a 30% upfront payment and net60 on the remainder. For credit mitigation require finance to run customer credit check and require a PO signed by procurement + an internal revenue holdback clause.
- Contractual protections: Include revenue clawback for 12 months on any MDF/co-fund credits; include minimum committed spend bands per year and an early termination adjustment.
- Contingency: Require Marketing commitment (co-marketing plan) to be signed and measurable; legal to approve all PR/case study language.

Attachments: Draft_Private_Offer_20261021.json (redlines included), NovaRetail_Pricing_Summary.pdf

Please see the impact summary below (high level):
- Year 1 recognized ARR forecast: $1.2M gross; net to Redwood after recommended rev-share ~ $972k (before amortization adjustments and any clawbacks).
- Cash timing: With 30% upfront we mitigate most short-term cash risk; balance on net60 helps bridge credit review.
- Sales value: Strategic retail anchor for our GCP channel; heavy co-sell and potential to drive 2 large pipeline deals in Q1.

Asking for a succinct reply from Jonas (approve, approve w/ tweaks, or decline) so we can communicate back to procurement by EOD Friday.

—Marissa

Thanks team — I read the recommendation and the attachments. Approve the exception with the following required conditions (no deviations without another exec review):

1) Finance & Legal controls: Finance must complete a credit review and sign off on the PO structure. Legal must insert a 12-month clawback on co-funded credits and an explicit early-termination revenue reconciliation clause.

2) Payment mitigation: Require 30% upfront at signing. Remaining balance net60 (not net90). If Finance flags material credit risk, require a standby letter of credit or a higher upfront percentage.

3) Performance milestones: Embedded minimum spend bands per year in the SOW; if bands not met a rev-share recalculation triggers and any marketing credits are subject to clawback.

4) Approval window & execution path: This signoff is valid for 72 hours. After that the deal must be re-presented. Please prepare the DocuSign-ready private offer with the above clauses and route to me for a quick sign. Marissa, coordinate with Legal and Finance and put the final DocuSign link in HubSpot.

Jonas
